text: "Innocence", is a South Korean film released in 2020. Directed by Park Sang-hyun, starring Shin Hye-sun, Bae Jong-ok, and Heo Joon-ho. The story tells that the mother (played by Bae Jong-ok) is suspected of adding pesticides to the rice wine at the funeral, causing many people to die, and her daughter (played by Shin Hye-sun), who is a lawyer, has to reverse the case for her mother.
"Gardenia Blossoms" is the first single released by He Jiong, a mainland Chinese host, in his capacity as a singer, with lyrics and music created by Wu Luan, and was released on June 1, 2004.

The main components of wood vinegar are acetic acid, acetone, and methanol. It has been used as a commercial source of acetic acid. In addition, wood vinegar usually contains 80-90% water and about 200 kinds of organic compounds.
The LD50 of methylamine  is 2400mg/m3. Methylamine is also a Schedule I compound listed by the Drug Enforcement Administration  in the United States .
Entonox is a type of anesthetic gas, which is a mixture of 50% nitrous oxide and 50% oxygen. Entonox is often used in pre-hospital emergency care, childbirth, and emergency situations.
Polyiodide refers to the polyatomic anions composed of multiple iodine atoms, which is a type of polyhalogen anions. Polyiodides refer to compounds containing polyiodide ions.

The main components of rubies and sapphires are both alumina, which show different colors due to other impurities. Rubies contain chromium oxide and appear red, while sapphires contain iron oxide and titanium dioxide and appear blue.
Thiol refers to a type of alcohol analogue in which the oxygen of alcohol is replaced by selenium. The most famous one is the amino acid selenocysteine.

Generally speaking, lithium oxide is produced by the combustion of lithium in the air. Due to the strong polarizing ability of lithium, the main product of the combustion reaction is lithium oxide, with very little lithium peroxide produced.

Iodoethane can be prepared by the reaction of red phosphorus, anhydrous ethanol, and iodine. In this reaction, phosphorus triiodide is unstable and needs to be generated in situ. The reaction temperature needs to be controlled.

Among the isotopes of hydrogen, the hydrogen isotopes with mass numbers 1-3 can be represented by a Chinese character like an element. The number of strokes in the lower left corner of "气" corresponds to the mass number.

Copper fluoroborate is a divalent copper salt of fluoroboric acid, which contains two fluoroboric acid anions. The shape of the fluoroboric acid anion is tetrahedral, similar to methane. The central boron atom has a negative charge because it forms four covalent bonds. Its oxidation state is +3.

Trifluoroacetic acid has multiple preparation routes: 1. Obtained by oxidizing 3,3,3-trifluoropropene with potassium permanganate. 2. Acetic acid  undergoes electrochemical fluorination with hydrofluoric acid, sodium fluoride, etc., and then obtained by hydrolysis.
Platinum oxide can be obtained by heating platinum dioxide to about 400°C: 2PtO2→2PtO+O2↑. Platinum oxide can also be obtained by heating platinum hydroxide: Pt2→PtO+H2O↑.

"Unchanging You is Good" is the 4th single of Japanese female singer Mayonaka Okamoto. It was released on January 16, 1997. It is the theme song of the 1996 TBS series drama "Return of Second Chance" . It was later used as an advertising song for the "SHINKIN BANK" of the Credit Cooperative. It ranked 8th in the Oricon Public Trust Singles Weekly Chart and won the Platinum Record Certification of the Japan Record Association.
"Nurses"  is a Colombian television series, which was broadcasted on RCN TV on October 23, 2019.
"Phoenix Button" is a Vietnamese costume drama directed by Huang Junying and was broadcast in 2020. It started airing on the streaming service POPS TV from March 5, 2020.
"Love is Around You" is a Malaysian drama co-produced by ntv7 and Mediacorp, unlike other co-produced dramas between Singapore and Malaysia, this drama is shot with a brand new script.
"Brothers and Sisters", an American TV series, depicts the story of a high-class family in Los Angeles, California, and has won an Emmy Award.

"Brilliant Heritage", a daily drama broadcasted by South Korea's KBS1TV from April 20, 2020, is co-created by director Kim Hyeong-il of "President" and writer Kim Kyung-hee of "Sweet Secret". The drama tells the story of a penniless 33-year-old single woman who pretends to marry an 80-year-old billionaire, and overnight becomes the stepmother of four sons, and their story of overcoming prejudice.

"From Heaven" is a romantic comedy science fiction film from China in 2015, directed by Wei Nan and Wei Min, produced by Zhang Ziyi and Guo Jingming, and starred by Chen Xuedong, Zhang Yixing, Jiang Wen, and Li Xiaolu.

"Stand Up" is the eighth single of Japanese singer Mai Kuraki, released on April 18, 2001. It initially sold 200,000 copies and accumulated sales of 470,000, making it the fourth highest-selling single in her career. Hideo Togenya was responsible for the composition and arrangement of the A-side "Stand Up", marking his first time in charge of the composition and arrangement of Mai Kuraki's A-side song.

Mushrooms and bitter oranges from the agriculture, forestry and fishery industry are famous specialties of Oita Prefecture. The mushrooms have star-shaped marks on the top, so they are often ranked in the top few in the national dried mushroom selection in Japan. For the fishery part, high-grade fish such as yellowtail, bluefin tuna, and flounder are the main. The governor of Oita Prefecture, Hiratsu Morihiko, once advocated the activity of "one village, one product", so each town and village in the county has its own specialty. Recently, with the agglomeration of automobile-related industries in Miyawaka City and Kanda Town in Fukuoka Prefecture, the northern part of Oita Prefecture, which is close to this area, has gradually become an automobile industry agglomeration area. In 2004, Daihatsu Motor began to assemble and manufacture in Nakatsu City.

Zunhua Chestnut Liquor is a kind of white liquor produced in Zunhua, Hebei, originated from the liquor brewed by local people Gao Qingcheng in the late Kangxi years. Gao Zhenye, the son of Gao Qingcheng, inherited his father's business and tried to brew liquor with the locally abundant chestnuts, which took seven years to succeed. In 2004, Gao Yonghai, the seventh generation descendant of chestnut liquor, established a private enterprise and resumed the production of chestnut liquor according to the ancestral secret recipe, and four years later, he reformed and expanded production to this day. Zunhua Chestnut Liquor is made from chestnuts as the main ingredient, and is brewed through the traditional craft that has been selected as a city-level intangible cultural heritage.

Gujeolpan is an appetizer in ancient Korean court cuisine, which can also refer to the container for this dish. It is a traditional Korean dish where 9 kinds of food are placed in a octagonal box with 9 compartments. In the middle of Gujeolpan, a thin pancake is usually placed, and the surrounding 8 compartments are filled with egg white strips, egg yolk strips, carrot strips, stir-fried beef strips, stone ear strips, cucumber strips, bean sprouts, mushroom strips, etc., according to the five flavors and five colors. The taste is mainly light, and the ingredients are freely matched and placed on the thin pancake roll, served with soy sauce, mustard or chili sauce. In modern Korean society, Gujeolpan has become a dish for Korean New Year or wedding banquets, but it is often simplified to a thin pancake with 6 kinds of ingredients, called Chiljeolpan.

tail.text: thin pancake with 6 kinds of ingredients

text: The Australian aboriginal bread has a history of thousands of years in Australia. This tradition gradually disappeared when the pre-ground white flour from Europe arrived in Australia. Bread making is a traditional women's job. It involves collecting seasonal grass or dried fruits. These are the materials they prepare for making flour. Because it is labor-intensive work, several ladies are required to participate each time.

Cheese is a major agricultural product worldwide. According to the data from the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, the world produced over 20 million tons of cheese in 2011, equivalent to about three kilograms per person. The largest cheese-producing country in the world is the United States, accounting for about 26% of the world's production, followed by Germany and France. The cheese produced in the United States is mainly mozzarella and cheddar, far more than other types of cheese.

Andong Soju is produced in Andong, its history can be traced back to the period of the Mongol invasion of the Goryeo Dynasty. It is brewed using traditional rice distillation techniques, with an alcohol content of 45 degrees, and was designated as an intangible cultural heritage of Gyeongsangbuk-do, South Korea in 1987.

Soyuz TMA-02M is one of the Russian Soyuz TMA series spacecraft, and the second improved Soyuz TMA-M series spacecraft. The spacecraft, carrying three astronauts, was successfully launched at 21:12 UTC on June 7, 2011, from the Baikonur launch site in Kazakhstan, heading for the International Space Station.
"Garfield's Fun Fest" is a 2008 American computer-animated film.
"Don't you see!", is the 19th single of the Japanese rock band ZARD, released on January 6, 1997.
"Eat"  is an underground American film directed by Andy Warhol in 1964.
"Devil" is a digital single by the South Korean girl music group CLC, planned by Cube Entertainment and released on September 6, 2019.
"Go Back to Your Alma Mater!" is the 21st single of the Japanese girl idol group NMB48, released by laugh out loud!records on August 14, 2019.

text: "Cats and Peachtopia" is a Chinese animated comedy film directed and written by Wang Wei in 2018, produced by Light Chaser Animation. It premiered in the People's Republic of China on April 5, 2018.

"Carnivorous Plant Research Society Magazine" is a Japanese quarterly journal and the official publication of the Japanese Carnivorous Plant Research Society. The magazine was founded in January 1950. As of 2010, it is published in A4 format with a total of 120 pages per year. In April 1986, the English name began to be used in conjunction with the Japanese name. Its typical content includes horticultural information, field investigation reports, literature reviews, and descriptions of new taxa and horticultural species. The text is usually in Japanese, but species descriptions may also be in English.
"Salvador Dali" is an American experimental film directed by Andy Warhol in 1966.
"Black Triangle" is an anti-espionage film produced by China Beijing Film Studio, which was released in 1977.
"Blue Punch" is the third mini album by the South Korean girl music group Rocket Punch, which will be released on August 4, 2020. The album includes 6 songs, with "Juicy" as the lead single.
"Bessatsu FRIEND" is a monthly girls' comic magazine published by Kodansha in Japan, which was founded in 1965 and is issued on the 13th of each month.
"Galaxy Science Fiction Novels" is a short science fiction novel magazine from the United States, published from 1950 to 1980.
"Purple Night" is the seventh single released by South Korean singer Sunmi on June 29, 2020, under MakeUS Entertainment.
"OH MY LOVE" is the 5th album of the Japanese band ZARD. It was released on June 4, 1994.

"Silver-haired Akide" is a theatrical animation work by the Japanese animation production company GONZO. It was released in Japan on January 7, 2006. This film was broadcast on the public television station and Dongsen Movie Channel in 2011.

text: "It's a Wonderful Life" is a Chinese TV drama produced by Mediacorp TV Singapore.

"NONSTOP" is the seventh mini album of the South Korean girl singing group Oh My Girl, with "NONSTOP" as the title track.
"Shinjuku Swan" is a Japanese comedy film from 2015, directed by Sion Sono, and adapted from the Japanese manga "Shinjuku Swan" by Ken Hikui. The film was released in Japan on May 30, 2015.

Martin varnish is a kind of clear varnish invented by the Martin brothers in Paris, France in 1728, imitating the oriental varnish of China and Japan. The cost of this varnish is much lower than that of the varnish imported from the East, and it is widely used.
Transparent Turquoise: Transparent turquoise crystals. Extremely rare and very valuable, currently only produced in Virginia, USA, with a single transparent gem weighing less than 1 carat;

Tianming Tongbao was a currency issued during the reign of the Later Jin ruler Nurhaci, named after Nurhaci's era name "Tianming". It was first minted in the first year of Tianming , and was divided into Manchu and Chinese versions, with the Manchu version being of higher quality than the Chinese one. The Manchu version is also referred to as "Tianming Khan Money", while Tianming Tongbao specifically refers to the Chinese version. The inscription on the Tianming Khan Money is in old Manchu.

The 7TP tank  was a light tank used by Poland during World War II. It was developed from the British Vickers six-ton tank, and its armament was significantly superior to its main competitors - the German No. 1 and No. 2 tanks. Although it performed well in the war with Germany in 1939, its production quantity was too small, less than 150 vehicles, and its chassis was used to manufacture the C7P artillery tractor.

The Gayageum is a traditional plucked string instrument from the Korean Peninsula, evolved from the ancient Chinese zither. It has been passed down from the Silla era, with a history of over 1500 years, and comes in various types, including twelve strings, fifteen strings, seventeen strings, eighteen strings, twenty-one strings, and twenty-five strings.

Fried spiders are a local snack in Cambodia. In Sukun Town, located in Zengborei County, Pongzhan Province, the spectacle of selling fried spiders as a specialty snack on the street has become a local attraction for tourists passing through this small town.

Ancient Well Roast Goose is a roast goose flavor made in Ancient Well Town, Xinhui, Guangdong, with a unique taste and great fame in Guangdong, almost representing Cantonese roast meat. Ancient Well Town in Xinhui City also uses "Ancient Well Roast Goose" as an advertising slogan to attract diners, hoping to attract more tourists from the Pearl River Delta to visit Ancient Well Town. The Ancient Well Roast Goose was originally made by using abandoned ancient wells as roasting facilities to roast the goose, which is rarely used today, and is replaced by modern gas and electric ovens.

PSM is a self-defense pistol designed by the Soviet Union Federal Instrument Design Bureau in 1969, intended for use by law enforcement agencies and officers. The gun was officially put into production at the Izhevsk Mechanical Plant in 1973.

text: The Makassar-class dock landing ship is a type of dock landing ship, originally designed by Daewoo Shipbuilding of South Korea for the Indonesian Navy, named after the Indonesian city of Makassar, with the first ship commissioned in 2007. The Peruvian Navy calls this class of ship the Pisco-class, the Philippine Navy calls it the Tarlac-class, and the medical ship specially built by Indonesia is called the Dr. Wahidin Sudirohusodo-class.

Yapana shoes are traditional sandals in Myanmar, similar to flip-flops. Although it refers to the sandals worn by almost all Burmese people, it is mainly used to refer to the traditional Mandalay velvet slippers originated in Upper Myanmar. The literal meaning of Hnyat-phanat is "clip shoes", because the slippers are fixed by clamping with the thumb and the second toe.

Mazda Flair is a light high-top travel car, which has been OEM produced by Suzuki Motor since October 2012 and labeled with Mazda's emblem. This car is developed based on Suzuki Wagon R and is only sold in the Japanese domestic market. This car is the successor of AZ-Wagon and is also in the same series as Flair Wagon.

"Prosecution Storm" is a crime court-themed movie in 2023. It is co-produced by the Film and Television Center of the Supreme People's Procuratorate and Wento Holdings, directed by Mai Zhaohui, produced by Tian Qiwen, and starred by Huang Jingyu, Bai Baihe, and Wang Likun, with special appearances by Wang Qianyuan and Feng Shaofeng. The film started shooting on July 28, 2020 in Dongguan and wrapped up on September 21. It premiered on April 29, 2023.

text: "Hungry Ghost Sarlo" is a robot animation produced by Sunrise Animation, which was broadcasted by Osaka TV Station and Tokyo TV Station from October 4, 1998 to March 28, 1999, with a total of 25 episodes. The director is Ryosuke Takahashi, the original author of "Armored Cavalry".

"Dracula" (English: Dracula) is an American TV series created by Cole Hutton, based on the famous novel "Dracula". On July 24, 2012, the National Broadcasting Company announced that it would skip the pilot episode and directly order 10 episodes of the show.

"Dates" is a British romance TV series, each episode tells the story of the first date of people who met online, exploring the "excitement and disaster" of the first date. The show was created by Bryan Elsley, who is also the creator of "Skins". The 9-episode show began airing on Channel 4 from June 10, 2013.

Phosphorus trisulfide, with the chemical formula P4S3, appears as a yellow solid and is one of the two methods used in industry to produce phosphorus pentoxide. Depending on the purity, the sample can present different colors from yellow-green to gray. Phosphorus trisulfide was first discovered by G.Lemoine, and its industrial production method was developed and produced in the Olbricht and Wilson laboratories in 1898. It dissolves in carbon disulfide of equal mass. Unlike other phosphorus sulfides, the hydrolysis of phosphorus trisulfide is slow and has a definite melting point.

A jet boat is a small boat propelled by a jet of water ejected from the stern. Unlike motorboats or motorboats that use external propellers in the water under or behind the boat, jet boats draw water from the bottom of the boat into the onboard water pump through the water inlet, and then discharge it through the nozzle at the stern. Modern jet boats were developed by New Zealand engineer Sir William Hamilton in the mid-1950s.

The Smith & Wesson Sigma is a series of semi-automatic pistols developed and produced by the American firearms company Smith & Wesson. It is the company's first attempt to use synthetic materials in firearm construction, and the grip is made of high-strength polymer materials. The Sigma can fire a variety of different pistol bullets. Its design and operation are similar to the Glock safe maneuvering pistol, which has led to some controversy and speculation about the patent legality of the gun.

Silver hexafluorophosphate is a common inorganic and organometallic chemical reagent. It is often used to provide weakly coordinating hexafluorophosphate anions to replace halide ligands; the reaction is driven by the formation of the corresponding silver halide precipitate. For example, in acetonitrile solution, the preparation of acetonitrile complexes from metal bromides usually involves a reaction.

Aluminum is a good conductor of electricity and heat, while aluminum oxide is an insulator for electricity and heat. The crystal form of aluminum oxide, corundum, is suitable for use as a grinding material and cutting tool due to its high hardness.

Silver phosphate precipitate not only has an important position in analytical chemistry, but it is also used in silver staining of biological materials  - as an indicator of phosphates. In early photography, silver phosphate was also found to be used as a photosensitizer. In 2010, there were reports that as a photocatalyst for the decomposition of water in visible light, silver phosphate has a high quantum yield , and can also be used to produce reactive oxygen in the same way. Silver phosphate is also a potential material that can add the antibacterial properties of silver ions to other materials.

Common emulsifiers include: surfactants, those with a high oil-water balance coefficient, suitable for preparing water-in-oil emulsions; those with a low oil-water balance coefficient, suitable for preparing oil-in-water emulsions; natural emulsifiers are mostly hydrophilic gums, which can increase the viscosity of the continuous phase, enhance the stability of the emulsion, and are suitable for preparing water-in-oil emulsions, solid particle emulsions, and auxiliary emulsifiers.

Acrylic resin is a group of thermoplastic or thermosetting plastic materials derived from acrylic acid. Methyl acrylic acid or other related compounds polymerize to form polymethyl acrylate, which can be used in acrylic resin paint, textile finishing agents, adhesives, bonding with clay, and correcting paper errors. Another type of acrylic resin is polymethyl methacrylate, which is used to improve the transparency of various hard plastics.

Androstenediol is a relatively weak endogenous androgen, and it is also an intermediate product of testosterone biosynthesis from dehydroepiandrosterone . Androstenediol and Androstenedione  have similar names, but note that the positions of their carbon-carbon double bonds are different.

Nitrous oxide is a kind of combustion-supporting agent, initially used to help German aircraft quickly escape from the battlefield during World War II, and now used in modified cars for straight-line acceleration.
About 2500 tons of Antimony trioxide are produced each year, which can be used as a coloring agent for glass or ceramics, and can also be used to manufacture glass with special requirements.

text: Copper hydroxide can convert acyl azide to carboxylic acid at room temperature. This can be used to synthesize some carboxylic acids with reactive functional groups. The yield is relatively high when using this method to prepare benzoic acid and octanoic acid.

text: Optical glass is the main material for manufacturing optical lenses and optical instruments. Optical glass must have a highly accurate refractive index, Abbe number, high transparency, and high uniformity.

tail.text: manufacturing optical lenses and optical instruments

text: Naphthalene is used for the production of dyes, resins, solvents, explosives, disinfectants, insecticides, preservatives, mothproofing agents, and carbide lighting gas. The catalytic oxidation of naphthalene can produce phthalic anhydride.

text: Tripe is a Chinese snack made from fresh bovine and ovine stomach, which is popular in northern regions such as Beijing, Tianjin, and Hebei. The specific method is to cook the finely cut parts of the bovine and ovine stomach in boiling water, hot oil, or hot soup, and eat it with sesame sauce, black vinegar, scallions, chili oil, and other dips. Tripe is divided into two major categories according to the materials: bovine stomach and ovine stomach, and it is divided into water explosion, oil explosion, soup explosion, and others according to the production methods. Water explosion is the main method in Beijing, Tianjin, and Hebei.

Wheat is rich in starch, protein, fat, minerals, calcium, iron, thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, etc. Due to different varieties and environmental conditions, the nutritional components vary greatly. From the perspective of protein content, the wheat grains grown in continental arid climate zones are hard and transparent, with a higher protein content, reaching 14 to 20%, and the gluten is strong and elastic, suitable for baking bread; the wheat grains grown in humid conditions contain 8 to 10% protein, the grains are soft, the gluten is poor, which shows that the geographical climate has a very important impact on the formation process of the product.

The most common sports bras today are similar to a vest that has been cut in half, made from fibers with high stretchability and good sweat absorption , and there are also products designed with colloids, water pads, and airbags. After some surgeries, some women also choose to wear sports bras to fix their breasts for wound healing. The straps of ordinary bras cause some women to feel tense when doing arm-lifting exercises, because the fixed bra is stretched, directly pressing on the trapezius muscle, which may eventually lead to symptoms such as shoulder numbness or pain. Sports bras are tied at the back so they can avoid this problem.

The Audi A8 is a standard luxury car produced by the German Audi. It is also the top model in the Audi brand. Its main competitors are the BMW 7 Series, Mercedes-Benz S-Class, Lexus LS, Toyota Crown, Honda Mileage, Nissan Fuga, Jaguar XJ, etc. It is the first car in the same class to use a lightweight all-aluminum alloy body, and there are multiple engines that can be matched with four-wheel drive for car owners who value handling or live in snowy areas. In 1996, an upgraded version of the A8, the Audi S8, was also produced.

Tom Yum , is a famous Thai hot and sour soup, made from galangal, tamarind, lemongrass, green onion, sour lemon, chili and fish sauce. The most common cooking method is to add shrimp and straw mushrooms, season with fish sauce and form a milky texture of Tom Yum Kung. There are also hot and sour chicken soup, hot and sour seafood soup, hot and sour coconut milk soup, etc.

Mapo Tofu is one of the representatives of Sichuan cuisine in Chinese dishes, highlighting the "numbing and spicy" characteristics of Sichuan cuisine. The main ingredients include tofu, minced beef, bean paste, and Sichuan peppercorns, etc. Among them, the numbing taste comes from Sichuan peppercorns, and the spicy sensation comes from chili peppers. Mapo Tofu is very popular worldwide, and its spiciness is often reduced accordingly, and it is modified with local seasonings.
Beef offal noodles is a snack originated from Xiangyang, Hubei. Beef offal refers to the internal organs of a cow, mainly referring to beef intestines and beef lungs  in Xiangyang.

Fleece is often used to make jackets, hats, sweaters, sweatpants, diapers, sportswear, hoodies, blankets, high-performance outdoor clothing, bedding, carpets, coats, vests, trench coats, gloves, scarves, hats, pillows, cushions, etc. Some of its production materials use recycled plastic bottles, and it is very soft, light, and easy to clean.
MP-472 "Vintuk" is a non-lethal handgun that fires 10x23mm T-caliber rubber bullets. The magazine capacity is 16 rounds, and the grip is made of blue plastic.

The city-wide computer cleaning day is organized annually in collaboration with the Cyber Crime Prevention Group, the Government Information Technology Director's Office, and the Hong Kong Computer Security Incident Coordination Center, aiming to enhance the security awareness of information technology in Hong Kong society, encourage the public to "clean" computers, and provide practical network security advice to computer users.

The Whitehead Mark5 torpedo is a Whitehead torpedo adopted by the United States Navy in 1910 as an anti-surface warship torpedo. The Mk5 torpedo is the first torpedo produced by a foreign company, the British Whitehead factory, and manufactured by the United States Navy Torpedo Station located in Newport, Rhode Island in 1908. It is also the first torpedo that allows the launching ship to adjust its range and speed.
